Shophouse Window Tinting
Is window film worth it for a shophouse?

Yes — street-level shophouses take the full force of the sun on the frontage with no shade and no setback, so the shopfloor gets very hot by afternoon. Quality film rejects the heat and 99% of UV, keeping the shop cool, protecting stock and window displays from fade, and adding daytime privacy at street level. Safety film also holds the glass together against knocks, break-ins and storm debris — all without darkening the shopfront.
How much does shophouse window tinting cost in Thailand?

Installed film runs from ฿70/sq ft for carbon film up to ฿180/sq ft for premium sputtering, with safety film priced by thickness. A typical shophouse frontage is 80–200 sq ft of glass, so most projects fall between ฿5,600 and ฿36,000 depending on glass area and film tier. The exact figure is confirmed free during an on-site measurement.
Does safety film really hold the glass together?

Yes. Safety film is a thicker 0.4–0.8mm layer bonded to the inside of the glass. If the pane is smashed by an impact, a break-in attempt or storm debris, the film holds the shattered glass in place rather than letting it collapse into the shop — buying time and reducing injury and loss. It also adds heat and UV rejection at the same time.
Can I get daytime privacy without darkening the shop?

Yes. Daytime-privacy film reflects the brighter side, so in daylight passers-by can't see into your counter, back office or stockroom while you keep a clear view out to the street. It stays crystal clear from the inside and doesn't dim the shopfront. At night the effect reverses, so for after-hours privacy we pair it with blinds or a higher-privacy tier.
Can you install without closing the shop?

Yes. We work early, late or on your quiet day and finish most shopfronts in a single day. No glass is removed and there's no workshop visit, so you rarely lose a trading day. We schedule the install around your hours.
